newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica assessing options on Transnet pension debt.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica assessing options on Transnet pension debt.

text.p: The South African government was considering several options to ease the pension fund-related debt facing transport utility Transnet, Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said on Monday.
She told a media briefing that the Stride Commission had made several suggestions on how to ease the debt, which she said was hampering Transnet's abilitity to maintain and improve infrastructure.
The Finance Department was now considering the tax implications.
Transnet managing director Saki Macozoma confirmed that Transnet was paying 1.4 billion rand a year to service its debt, which had been run up to support its generous defined benefit pension fund.

The Stride Committee had recommended that its pensioners should be transferred to the state pension fund so that it could start with a clean slate, offering a more manageable defined contribution pension fund to existing staff.
If this happened, Transnet would shift from a position where it made a loss of 1.5 billion rand a year to making profits of between 800 million rand and one billion rand a year.
"We have to look how we can really help Transnet move forward and deal with its pension fund deficit," Macozoma said.
"What has been happening in the past is that Transnet has been existing to service the pension fund and consequently there has been a situation where we have not been able to replace assets.

"The consequence is that in the ports we have to invest so much money...Spoornet needs about 1.5 billion rand for the next 10 years just to be able to restructure because we have not been servicing that infrastructure."
